new_packages.label_en: The Path of God and His Testimonies
new_packages.reason: The second new package for this Torah, representing the good/holy pole. The source text equates 'דֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ' (the path of God) with 'עֵדוֹתֶיךָ' (Your testimonies) through the identical verbal structure 'לֹא נָטִיתִי / לֹא נָטָה' — both phrases use the same root (נָטָה, to turn/deviate) to describe the same refusal. These two nodes form an independent domain of divine anchorage — the spiritual ground a person holds when facing controversy.

observations:
Torah 258 is one of the shortest Torahs in Likutay Moharan Volume 1 — essentially one sentence of principle followed by one proof text. It is entirely absent from torahData.js (reference 258 does not appear in the dataset at all).

The Torah teaches a single aphoristic principle: controversy (machloket) directed against a person can sway him from God's path and cause him to fall from his level. David the King is cited as the paradigmatic case of one who faced great opposition and yet remained anchored.

Despite its brevity, the Torah contains two clear bechina equivalences:
1. (Evil domain) Machloket = 'rodoفai v'tzarai' — controversy IS the pursuers and adversaries. The 'וְזֶה שֶׁהִתְפָּאֵר' construction is the Rebbe's standard 'this is a bechina of' marker.
2. (Good domain) Derech Hashem = 'edutekha' — God's path IS His testimonies. The Rebbe paraphrases the verse's 'edutekha' as 'derech Hashem' in his closing gloss, establishing their identity.

These yield two minimal packages (2 nodes each) with a perfect good/evil mirror structure:
- Package 1 (evil): machloket / pursuers-and-adversaries — the hostile external force
- Package 2 (good): derech Hashem / edutekha — the divine anchor

The verdict is NEW_PACKAGES_PROPOSED because Torah 258 is completely absent from torahData.js — the entire Torah needs to be encoded from scratch, with 2 packages and 2 bechina edges.

The eitza chain (machloket → hayyah from God's path → nefilah from one's level) is the practical logic of the teaching but does not generate additional bechina packages. 'Hayyah' and 'nefilah' are eitza consequences, not conceptual domains with their own parallel-nature clusters.

Note on connection to Torah #251: Torah #251 also discusses machloket and its spiritual dangers. In that Torah, the evil of machloket operates through 'machshavot kefirah' (thoughts of heresy), and the positive response involves 'mesirat hamilchamah l'Hashem' and 'emet.' Torah #258 presents a compressed version of the same essential teaching — controversy threatens one's standing — but in a single sentence without the extended argument of Torah #251. The two Torahs are distinct packages; each stands on its own. Cross-Torah: the node 'מחלוקת' from Torah #258 may share its node_id with machloket nodes in other Torahs, serving as a bridge in cross-Torah traversal.
